latency: p99, whiskers p50 to p99.9
QoS 1, 16 B, MQTT 5 (rumqttd 3.1.1). Each publisher sends on a fixed schedule; the offered rate counts deliveries. Steps run 2 s, then measure 8 s, on the same connections.
Latency runs from the send to delivery, or from when it was due if the broker held it back. Seconds with host CPU steal are left out. Broker on CPUs 0-3, load generator on CPUs 4-5.
A step fails under 95% delivered, on a closed connection, or at a median over 100 ms; a cross marks it and no higher step runs.
A broker that drops clients while they connect fails its first step with 0% delivered. Fan-out latency includes the generator reading each burst of 1000 deliveries.
Tuned configs, except where they run out of memory at 20K connections: NanoMQ's queue (2048), FluxMQ's send queue (1000), VerneMQ's socket buffers (128 KiB). See COMPARISONS.md.
MQTT brokers at fixed load, TCP loopback
Intel Core i7-8700B @ 3.20 GHz (QEMU/KVM), performance governor, turbo off
point to point: 10K publishers → 10K subscribers, a topic each (20K connections)
fan-in: 10K publishers → a shared subscription of 100
